parts.label: c
parts.text: A tidal basin covers 1.0 × 10⁶ m² with a tidal range of 4.0 m. Water density is 1000 kg m⁻³. Estimate the gravitational energy available per tide and the maximum daily mean power for two generating tides per day.

answer.text: Bohr assigns definite circular orbits with quantised angular momentum; Schrödinger describes the electron by a wavefunction and probability distribution, without a definite trajectory. Bohr’s allowed angular momenta give discrete energies. In the wave model, acceptable stationary wavefunctions and boundary conditions allow only discrete energies. The wave model explains more detailed spectra and electron distributions and extends beyond hydrogen, whereas the simple Bohr model has a much narrower range.

answer.text: Some wave energy passes the device or is reflected; friction, turbulence and electrical resistance also transfer energy to the surroundings. The conversion efficiency is therefore below 100%.
